newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Ung Huot says will accept premier post.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Ung Huot says will accept premier post.

text.p: Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot said on Wednesday he was willing to accept the job of first prime minister, replacing the ousted Prince Norodom Ranariddh as Hun Sen's coalition partner.

Ung Huot, a senior member of First Prime Minister Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party, said he would keep his job as foreign minister. He also said he still respected Ranariddh but put the interests of the country first.

"I accept to be first prime minister because I put the interests of my people and my country first," Ung Huot told reporters. "The interests of the country dictate that Cambodia must go on ... We cannot wait. We've suffered too much."

Hun Sen overthrew Ranariddh on July 6 after a weekend of fighting in the capital but said he wanted the coalition between his Cambodian People's Party (CPP) and the royalist FUNCINPEC to remain in place and for FUNCINPEC to choose a new first prime minister to replace Ranariddh.

Ung Huot's nomination will be forwarded to the National Assembly when it reopens on July 28. Earlier on Wednesday, FUNCINPEC officials said they had agreed on Ung Huot's nomination for the first prime minister post.
The CPP would support Ung Huot's nomination in the National Assembly, an adviser to Hun Sen said.
"We ... can support him in the National Assembly, to adopt him," Hun Sen adviser Om Yentieng told Reuters. "We feel that he is acceptable."
Earlier on Wednesday, another leading candidate for the post of first prime minister said he could not take the job because he was not a member of parliament.
Toan Chay, leader of a dissident faction of Ranriddh's FUNCINPEC party had been tipped to replace Ranariddh as Hun Sen's co-premier.
"I can't accept the premiership because ... I am not a member of parliament. I am only the governor of a province, and His Majesty the King asked that the constitution not be amended," he said.
Toan Chay, the governor of Siem Reap province who broke with Ranariddh in April, said he welcomed Ung Huot's nomination.
"This is very good because Ung Huot is considered to be a neutral person who we trust with our destiny over the next year," he said, referring to Cambodia's next election due in May 1998.
Many FUNCINPEC members left the country in the aftermath of Ranariddh's ousting and the killing of at least two senior party officials.

Ranariddh, who left the country the day before Hun Sen's forces moved against the prince's troops in the capital, has called for resistance to Hun Sen and appealed to the international community for support.

The prince has pleaded his case in meetings with French and Japanese envoys in Paris, U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan in New York, and U.S. State Department officials and members of Congress in Washington, as well as in telephone calls from the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).
But apart from a sympathetic hearing and advice to try to make peace with Hun Sen, the prince has received no firm offers of support.
